image_prompt.text: Scattered shipping crates, concrete barricades, and metal barriers — waist-high (3–4 studs) and full-body (7–8 studs) — distributed evenly across every lane
Two mirrored team bases at opposite ends of the industrial yard, walled off from the sniper towers' firing lines
Narrow transitions where the symmetrical lanes meet — alley mouths and gaps between the buildings — concentrating fights into contested ground
Sniper towers at opposite ends of the map, plus steel catwalks and elevated platforms spanning between buildings, reachable only through exposed, predictable stairs and ladders
Multiple concrete-and-metal warehouse buildings entered from the street through doorways, with window openings to fire out of
Modern industrial urban-warfare aesthetic throughout: poured concrete walls, corrugated and riveted metal, steel railings, rust and grime

layout_placement.text: Balanced team spawn zones at opposite ends, shielded from the sniper towers' sightlines
Expose wall height, building count, and cover density as tunable attributes on the generated map

notes: Medium-sized map; scale it for two teams rather than a large-player-count battlefield.
cover-elevated routes P2 rather than P0 + tiered because the catwalks overhang the floor below; if the catwalks are dropped in favour of solid tiered platforms it falls back to P0 + tiered.
building-interior adds P3 for the outside-to-inside transition.

Preset caveat: the prompt says 'tactical', but the genre notes' MilSim reading (breach-sequence raid site, no mirrored bases, clear-in-sequence) is contradicted by the requested symmetrical lanes, team-vs-team balance, and opposite-end bases. Team Deathmatch was taken instead; the Tactical Shooter preset was deliberately not used.
choke-bottleneck came in with the preset rather than being named in the prompt; it follows naturally from lanes converging, but drop it if the pipeline treats preset options as strictly opt-in.

Request no option covered: exposing wall height, building count, and cover density as tunable attributes. Emitted as free text in layout_placement, but it is a parameterisation request rather than a placed element.
No option enforces mirror symmetry; it is carried only as wording in the lane and spawn text. If lane-network generation does not guarantee a symmetric result, this needs handling downstream.

would have asked: whether to take the team deathmatch layout — mirrored bases at opposite ends, lanes between them, and cover through the middle — with the buildings, catwalks, and sniper towers added on top, or to build it up from scratch.
would have asked: whether the buildings should be genuinely enterable interiors (a slower build) or solid façades with window openings only, which would drop the P3 cost.
would have asked: anything else you want in the space?
